content: Be content, then, with being a philosopher in all things; and if you wish also to appear so to any one, appear so to yourself, and it will be enough.
author: Epictetus
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. We are conditioned to believe that more is always better—more possessions, more accomplishments, more stimulation. Yet our accumulation usually brings more anxiety, maintenance, and mental clutter.

In Epictetus's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Wealth is not having endless things; it is wanting very little. When you realize that your deepest needs for peace, connection, and purpose cannot be bought, you become truly unshakeable.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
